content.text: I'll query the SCOPe service info endpoint to get the current release and periodic update values.

content.thinking: The current-release endpoint shows SCOPe 2.08 as the stable release (frozen 2021-07-28, released 2021-09-22), with the latest periodic update being 2.08-2026-08-16.

answers.answer:
The current-release endpoint (/api/v1/releases/current) reports SCOPe release 2.08 as the current public stable release, with stable_label "2.08-stable". Its classification was frozen on 2021-07-28 and released on 2021-09-22. It is flagged is_public=true and is_comprehensive=false, meaning 2.08 does not attempt to classify every PDB entry. The latest periodic update is reported as version "2.08-2026-08-16", dated 2026-08-16.

For a reproducible analysis, cite the frozen stable release identifier, SCOPe 2.08 (2.08-stable), and pin all release-scoped API calls to release=2.08 (e.g. /api/v1/releases/2.08/...). The stable release is a fixed snapshot: its SUNIDs, SIDs, SCCS codes, domain boundaries, and ASTRAL subsets do not change, so results can be regenerated exactly by anyone citing that version. If a result depends specifically on newly added entries, cite the exact dated periodic label as well (2.08-2026-08-16), because a bare "2.08" does not identify which periodic snapshot was consulted.

The periodic label means the 2.08 stable framework (same hierarchy of classes, folds, superfamilies, and families, same curated manual assignments) has been incrementally extended by automated classification of newly released PDB entries that could be assigned by sequence/structure similarity to existing 2.08 nodes, as of the date embedded in the label. Periodic updates add new PDB entries, chains, and domains to existing nodes without re-curating the stable classification or adding new manually-curated folds/superfamilies. Because these labels change with each update (the date is the version), they are a moving target; citing one is only reproducible if the exact dated label is given, and the stable release remains the preferred reference. The periodic additions are automated and inherit the lineage of the node they are assigned to, so they should not be treated as curator-verified homology at the family/superfamily level; shared fold alone is not homology, and function should not be transferred from an automated assignment without additional evidence.
